title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Shipment Status Behind a Corrected Set
content:
Whether a corrected `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` set puts any originals into circulation depends in part on the booking behind the document. This page sets out the booking test.

## Rule

1. The booking behind the document passes the test when its status is loaded, departed or closed.
2. A status of gated in passes only where the document's type holds the received-for-shipment permission.
3. Only the booking record that belongs to the documentation party of the document is examined. If the booking reference leads to a booking held by some other customer, that booking is left unread and the test is failed.
4. If the booking is in any other status, the test is failed, and the corrected set sends no originals into circulation; the number is zero.

## Quick check

| Booking behind the document | Passes the booking test? |
|---|---|
| Documentation party's own booking, loaded | Yes |
| Documentation party's own booking, departed or closed | Yes |
| Documentation party's own booking, gated in, type with received-for-shipment permission | Yes |
| Documentation party's own booking, gated in, type without that permission | No |
| Documentation party's own booking, confirmed | No |
| Booking of another customer, whatever its status | No |

## Point of judgement

**The booking has closed since the vessel sailed. Does it still pass?** Yes. Closed is one of the qualifying statuses.
